Minbox text archive

Ask your phone AI about your text messages.

Use your own agent CLI on an always-on computer to build a filtered text archive. Then ask your preferred AI phone app useful questions about it.

Minbox provides reference code, setup guides, and lessons from real installations. Your agent does the technical work. You choose the privacy rules and AI service.

What you need first

  • An always-on computer with internet access and private storage.
  • An installed coding agent CLI with command access and a strong reasoning model.
  • Your messaging device or synchronized message source.
  • An AI phone account that supports the connection you choose.

A CLI is an assistant you run in a terminal. A chat subscription alone does not install it or supply every connection.

Start with the Minbox repository. Its README gives you a setup prompt for your agent.

The setup path

  1. Agree on which originals the setup agent may inspect and what the answering AI may receive.
  2. Connect your messages. Android/Linux uses a paired Google Messages collector. iPhone/Mac uses Messages synchronized to your Mac.
  3. Collect private originals and create a separate filtered archive.
  4. Connect your AI phone app through a suitable cloud connector, connected computer, or restricted search service.
  5. Ask one useful question from your phone and check its source. Your agent checks collection, filtering, and scheduled-job status.

Google Drive is one option. It is not required for every design. The supplied Drive path has the most complete setup recipe.

The local exporter needs an existing archive and correction ledger. A new installation without Drive needs agent adaptation.

Your privacy choices

Routine collection and full-archive filtering need no AI model calls. The supplied rules exclude authentication codes, recognizable reset links, and clear promotional spam.

A cloud setup agent can still receive originals through its tools. Broad computer access can let an answering app read beyond the filtered folder.

For stricter privacy, your agent can explore local-model filtering before releasing text to a cloud AI. That integration is not included. No filter detects every secret.

If you choose Drive

You choose a private folder and complete Google consent. Minbox requests drive.file for selected and app-created files.

This is per-file access, not recursive folder access. Minbox also checks the signed-in owner, private root, and managed parent folders.

Renaming the folder preserves its ID and connection. Unrelated files added to it are not automatically authorized or imported.

Your AI service needs separate access consent. Its permissions can cover more than the archive. Private messages are not published on this website.

Corrections and limits

A Corrections document records explicit changes, such as hiding spam. A personal label can exclude a message from a work view while retaining it in the full archive.

Collection covers accessible history, not a complete phone backup. Available original images can be verified and stored privately through the Drive path.

Optional local OCR extracts text from images and can make mistakes. Unsupported media and unavailable history remain gaps.

AI answers can omit context or be wrong. Check the source messages before relying on an answer.

Live Android/Linux operation has worked in an existing installation. New installations need their own checks. The Mac/iPhone path is fixture-tested; live operation still needs verification. Android collection on Mac or Windows is not implemented.

Keeping it working

Your agent schedules collection, filtering, output updates, and suitable health checks. Reviewed recovery handles ordinary failures.

Optional external email covers unresolved emergencies that need human action. It does not send routine, reminder, or recovery mail.

A local monitor cannot report a complete host or network outage. Check phone retrieval separately from local job health.
